subject: MAP: phased capacity backstop, evaluation gating, and GPU pool sizing
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenhealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@zenhealth.ai>
Date: 2025-08-14T09:15:00Z
Subject: Initial MAP request — capacity lead times and phased pool approach

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to start formalizing a Mutual Action Plan that covers dedicated/private capacity lead times and a phased GPU pool sizing for our pilot -> production ramp. High-level asks from our side:

- A MAP that shows an evaluation gate (KPIs) and the corresponding capacity tranches to reserve.
- Lead-time estimates for Dedicated (hosted + reserved) and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments — H100 vs A100 options.
- A recommended initial pool size for pilot (8–16 GPUs) and a growth path to full-prod (60–120 GPUs) based on 1M monthly requests.
- Backstop/fallback options if vendor procurement delays occur.

I attached a short scope doc to help frame expected throughput and compliance needs. Can your team put together a draft MAP with a proposed timeline and a couple sizing scenarios? We’re targeting a commercial close by end of Q4 2025.

Best,
Alex

Attachment: zenhealth-scope.pdf (1 page — expected concurrency, dataset notes, SOC2 required)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-14T10:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request — capacity lead times and phased pool approach

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear scope. Attaching an initial MAP draft (map-draft-v1.pdf) with three scenarios: conservative (pilot-first, small dedicated tranche), balanced (staggered reserve with burst capacity), and aggressive (commit to larger tranche with preferred pricing).

Quick clarifying questions to make the sizing practical:
- Target p99 latency SLA for production (ms)?
- Expected mix of short chat vs long context generation (avg tokens per request)?
- Any hard compliance constraints that require on-prem versus VPC?

We included a backstop strategy in the draft (short-term autoscale to hosted fallback + cached prefix layers) and proposed gating criteria for the eval (latency, cost per 1k requests, and hallucination error on a 100-case prompt set).

If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in Engineering for concrete lead-time estimates and a procurement cadence. Proposed next step: 30-min MAP review on Monday (Aug 18).

—Mateo

Attachment: map-draft-v1.pdf (4 pages — scenarios, gating KPIs, preliminary timeline)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenhealth.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-15T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP draft — technical sizing and lead-time notes

Adding technical context for the MAP draft. Notes below — feel free to paste into the doc.

- Hardware lead times (typical, subject to vendor stock): H100 (preferred for latency at scale) — 10–14 weeks lead time for dedicated procurement; A100 — 6–10 weeks. If ZenHealth needs Private on-prem, add 2–4 weeks for networking + on-site validation.
- Sizing heuristics (for 1M monthly requests):
  • Pilot (P.O.C) — 8 GPUs (A100) assuming aggressive batching, target p95 < 300ms.
  • Stage (10–20% traffic) — 24–32 GPUs (H100 preferred) with KV prefix cache to lower cost.
  • Prod (steady-state) — 60–100 GPUs (H100), or hybrid of 40 H100 + 40 quantized A100 nodes for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Backstop: maintain a 10–15 GPU hosted pool as spillover for short bursts; enable pre-warmed shards to reduce cold-start tail.
- Quantization: Mixed 4-bit quantized variants reduce cost ~2–3x but may need eval gating for quality regression.

Attaching a quick hardware-options spreadsheet. I recommend the MAP include a 6–8 week procurement buffer for any committed tranche and a clear sign-off milestone tied to a deposit schedule.

—Ben

Attachment: hardware-options.xlsx (spreadsheet — H100/A100 variants, perf numbers, lead-time estimates)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenhealth.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-16T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP draft — commercial sequencing and contractual milestones

Alex — from a commercial and procurement sequencing perspective, here’s a pragmatic MAP addition that smooths commitment risk: 

1) Milestone 1 (Eval gate, 2–4 weeks): validation of model quality on customer prompt set. No capacity commit.
2) Milestone 2 (Pilot commit, 30% discount optional, 4–8 weeks): reserve pilot tranche (8–24 GPUs) with refundable deposit that applies to first 3 months usage. Allow conversion to Dedicated or Private with a 6–8 week lead-time notice.
3) Milestone 3 (Scale commit, final close): commit to production tranche (60+ GPUs) with staggered delivery windows and pricing tiers. Add SLAs for availability and preemption protection.

I’ve attached a proposed timeline CSV that maps these milestones to dates and the proposed deposit/credit mechanics. Important to call out: deposits should allow a 30-day opt-out window before full procurement starts to protect both sides.

If we agree, we’ll bake these milestones into the MAP PDF and provide a short SOW + DocuSign for signature.

—Karthik

Attachment: mutual-action-timeline.csv (milestone, date windows, deposit %)
From: Procurement Team <procure@zenhealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenhealth.ai>
Date: 2025-08-18T16:08:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: acceptance of phased MAP and next steps for SOW

Hi Karthik / Mateo,

We reviewed the MAP draft and the proposed milestone cadence. Procurement is comfortable moving forward subject to:

- Final SOW with milestone-based payment schedule and a 30-day opt-out clause prior to hardware procurement.
- Confirmation of lead times in writing and a contingency plan for >14-week H100 delays.
- A clear list of compliance artifacts (SOC2 audit timeline, data residency controls for Private).

Please send the SOW + DocuSign link and we’ll route internally for signature. Targeting signature by Aug 29 so we can lock the pilot tranche.

Thanks —
Procurement Team
ZenHealth
